target.title: fix(msteams): bound probe token acquisition to request deadline
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Maintainer options</summary>

- Land-ready, no follow-up required
- Squashes cleanly onto `a788617325` (origin/main) — no rebase needed
- All sibling MS Teams call sites already use `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`; this PR brings the probe in line with the established pattern
- No new public API, no SDK surface change, no config / default / migration / protocol impact
- No issue filed; per ClawSweeper precedent #103185 / #106034, this is an additive defense fix in the "network layer bound" wave
- The test rewrite addresses the ClawSweeper P2 (automation) finding by replacing wall-clock waits with `vi.useFakeTimers()`. The scratchpad harness in section 4.2 addresses the P1 (needs proof) finding by exercising the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` + `@azure/msal-node` path against a stalled loopback `node:http` server.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

`probeMSTeams()` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89` awaits `tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` for the Bot Framework and Microsoft Graph token endpoints with no surrounding deadline. The Microsoft Teams SDK does not carry an inherent timeout on these calls, so a stalled Azure AD token endpoint pins the probe indefinitely. Six other MS Teams paths already wrap the same SDK calls with `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` (default `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`); the probe was the one missing site.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two probe awaits now mirror the established pattern in [`attachments/bot-framework.ts:252-256`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/bot-framework.ts) and [`attachments/graph.ts:258-262`](extensions/msteams/src/attachments/graph.ts) — wrap the SDK call in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` with a descriptive `label`. The default 30s bound is identical to the bound the sibling paths use. The method's contract is unchanged: a stalled SDK call now resolves with the same error shape that other paths already produce, and the existing `try/catch` blocks (the outer catch at `:138` for the bot token, the inner catch at `:110` for the graph token) convert the timeout into a `ProbeMSTeamsResult` with `ok: false` and a structured `error` field. No new helper is introduced; the fix reuses the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`.

**Fix classification: root cause fix.** No schema, default, migration, protocol, or provider behavior changes. No new public API or SDK surface.

## User Impact

Operators running `probeMSTeams()` (used by setup checks, health probes, and CI validation) no longer see the probe hang past 30s when Azure AD stalls. The bot token timeout surfaces as `ok: false, error: "<withMSTeamsRequestDeadline timeout message>"`; the graph token timeout surfaces as `graph: { ok: false, error: "..." }` while the rest of the probe still completes (the graph block has its own `try/catch`).

## Evidence

### 4.1 Focused vitest output — fake-timer rewrite

The committed regression guard at [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts) drives the **real** `probeMSTeams()` code path under `vi.useFakeTimers()` so the 30-second production deadline from `withTimeout` (`@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/timing.js:25`, uses `setTimeout`) resolves in milliseconds instead of waiting 30 wall-clock seconds per case. The wrapper behavior is asserted without paying deterministic CI cost.

Command:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

Result (5 cases, focused wall-clock 15.23s — transform + import only; tests themselves total 39ms):

```
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the bot token stalls 25ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when the graph token stalls 3ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns a bounded probe result when both tokens stall 2ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > returns ok=true for a normal (non-stalled) probe 1ms
 ✓ |extension-msteams| extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts > msteams probe request-deadline > uses the documented 30s production default deadline for both token acquisitions 2ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
   Start at  23:43:12
   Duration  15.23s (transform 8.40s, setup 557ms, import 14.38s, tests 39ms, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 21.72s
```

Per-case wall-clock after the first version of this PR: 90s of stalled-wait (`Promise.race` against a real `setTimeout` budget). After the rewrite: 25ms / 3ms / 2ms / 1ms / 2ms. The fifth case asserts the production default deadline is exactly `MSTEAMS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` by spying on `withTimeout`'s `timeoutMs` argument, so the production contract is not silently weakened by the fake-timer change.

### 4.2 Exact-head controlled MS Teams SDK transport proof

The P1 (real-SDK proof) finding is addressed by a temporary uncommitted harness that drives the production `probeMSTeams` entry point through the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` constructor and real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication.acquireTokenByClientCredential`. MSAL's outbound `fetch` calls (the OIDC discovery GET and the token POST to `https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/...`) are redirected via a `globalThis.fetch` monkey-patch to a local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` that selectively stalls. No mocked fetch adapter; no real Azure traffic; no credentials.

- Exact head: `082f48e96c04f9680b46029a392ac83d8264c1d2`
- Scope: production `probeMSTeams()` wrapper path → production `loadMSTeamsSdkWithAuth()` → real `@microsoft/teams.apps` `App` (token manager) → real `@azure/msal-node` `ConfidentialClientApplication` → `globalThis.fetch` (patched) → loopback `node:http` server. The wrapper `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` is the real production helper; the SDK, MSAL, and HttpClient are unmodified real packages.

Redacted command form actually run:

```bash
PROOF_HEAD=082f48e96c \
  HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= \
  NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost \
  /usr/bin/timeout 120s "$(command -v node)" --import tsx \
    scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts
```

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head=082f48e96 controlled local MS Teams SDK transport
entra-root: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>
client: starting real probeMSTeams() with redirected MSAL fetch
client: redirected body-stall https://login.microsoftonline.com/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
server: phase=body-stall POST /body-stall/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
client: phase=body-stall status=200 headers-sent
probe: bot elapsed=30002ms ok=false error=MS Teams Bot Framework probe token timed out after 30000ms
client: redirected normal-after https://login.microsoftonline.com/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
server: phase=normal-after POST /normal-after/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222/oauth2/v2.0/token
client: phase=normal-after status=200 headers-sent
probe: graph elapsed=17ms ok=false error=Invalid token specified: missing part #2
probe: total elapsed=30524ms
assertion: graph bounded within 35s = true
assertion: bot bounded within 35s = true
proof: server closed cleanly
shellExit=0
```

Observation:
- The real `@azure/msal-node` POSTed the Bot Framework token request to the redirected loopback server (the body-stall phase).
- The body-stall server sent headers, then never called `res.end()`. MSAL's reader waited on the body.
- The production `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` wrapper aborted the SDK call at the 30-second production default (`probe: bot elapsed=30002ms`, error matches the documented `withTimeout` format: `"<label> timed out after <ms>ms"`).
- The graph call attempt immediately after completed in 17ms against the normal-after phase (the fake JWT in the response intentionally has no second segment so MSAL rejects the parse — proves the second call is not poisoned by the first's abort and the wrapper's deadline doesn't leak across calls).
- Total wall-clock: 30.5s. Without the fix, the bot call would have hung indefinitely past the harness budget.
- The harness file (`scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts`) was deleted after the run; only the redacted transcript above survives in this PR body.

Known limits: this is controlled local SDK transport proof, not live Entra. The proxy env vars are set defensively in case the SDK spawns any other fetch (it did not in this run); MSAL constructs the token URL directly. Not tested: live Azure AD endpoint behavior, real Entra TLS, real MSAL production configuration, regional auth clouds, federated identity flow, managed identity flow.

### 4.3 What I checked

- **Current-main behavior**: stock-pinned `a788617325` (main) still has naked `await tokenProvider.getAccessToken(...)` at `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts:75` and `:89`; a never-settling promise leaves the probe pending indefinitely.
- **Proposed runtime repair**: PR head routes both token acquisitions through the existing `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` helper from `extensions/msteams/src/request-timeout.ts:34`, preserving the existing outer catch at `:138` and the graph-specific inner catch at `:110`.
- **Existing owner pattern**: the same `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline` helper is already in use at 8 sibling MS Teams sites (see the table in section 4.5). The probe was the one missing consumer; this PR brings it in line with the established pattern.
- **Test cost reduction**: the original committed test waited 90 seconds of wall-clock per focused run (3 stalled cases × 30s deadline); the rewrite uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` to drive the same `withTimeout` race in milliseconds, with one extra case asserting the production default is `30_000`.
- **P1 proof**: the `scratchpad/msteams-probe-real-sdk-proof.mts` harness (deleted after the run) drove the production `probeMSTeams` entry point through the real `@microsoft/teams.apps` App + real `@azure/msal-node` against a stalled loopback server. The transcript above shows the bounded 30-second abort and the recovery on the subsequent graph call.
- **Automated validation**: the existing GitHub context (lint, prod types, test types, extension-boundary checks, Node test shards, security-fast, Opengrep, real-behavior-proof workflow) all pass on the PR head; these supplement but do not replace the contributor proof.

### 4.4 Regression coverage

The committed [`extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts`](extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts) (4 tests) continues to pass — the fix preserves the existing happy-path, missing-credentials, token-error, and delegated-token behaviors:

```
 ✓  returns an error when credentials are missing                          3ms
 ✓  validates credentials by acquiring a token                              2ms
 ✓  returns a helpful error when token acquisition fails                    1ms
 ✓  reports delegated tokens expired when the process clock is invalid      2ms
```

### 4.5 Impact-surface review

`probeMSTeams` is the only consumer of `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` in `extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts`. Every other MS Teams path that calls `tokenProvider.getAccessToken` is already wrapped in `withMSTeamsRequestDeadline`:

| File:line | Label | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `attachments/bot-framework.ts:252` | `MS Teams Bot Framework token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `attachments/graph.ts:258` | `MS Teams Graph media token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:594` | `Teams media list` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:654` | `Teams graph token (for quote)` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:685` | `Teams graph token (for download)` | ✓ wrapped |
| `monitor-handler/message-handler.ts:692` | `Teams parent + replies` | ✓ wrapped |
| `attachments/download.ts:167` | `Teams attachment token` | ✓ wrapped |
| `team-identity.ts:37` | `Team identity lookup` | ✓ wrapped |
| **`probe.ts:75` (this PR)** | `MS Teams Bot Framework probe token` | **fixed** |
| **`probe.ts:89` (this PR)** | `MS Teams Graph probe token` | **fixed** |

The probe was the one missing site. No new helper, no new public API, no SDK change.

### 4.6 Sibling reference

This PR is part of the same network-layer "additive defense" wave:

- [#106034](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106034) `fix(google): bound realtime browser token requests` — Alix-007, MERGED 2026-07-13 — closest analog for the scratchpad proof shape (controlled local SDK transport via a temporary uncommitted harness with a real `node:http` server). Their pattern was followed here.
- [#106035](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106035) `fix(telegram): bound stalled diagnostic response reads` — Alix-007, open — body-read bound in `getMe`/`getWebhookInfo`/`getChatMember`. Their `vi.useFakeTimers()` + `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(...)` pattern in `extensions/telegram/src/probe.response-body-timeout.test.ts` was followed for the test rewrite here.
- [#106036](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106036) `fix(discord): bound stalled probe response reads` — Alix-007, open — body-read bound in Discord probe `getMe` JSON.

### 4.7 Verification commands

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts
node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 --config .oxlintrc.json \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.test.ts \
  extensions/msteams/src/probe.timeout.test.ts \
  --reporter=verbose
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json
```
